title: Rate sensitivity + quasi-static limit + thermal softening verification
objective: Phase 3 acceptance suite. Three unit-level tests that exercise the distinguishing features of viscoplasticity against closed-form or limiting-case expectations.
scope: Rate-sensitivity test: drive a single element at several strain rates; Perzyna and JC must show monotone stress-vs-rate curves.
Quasi-static limit test: at eps_dot -> 0, both models match rate-independent J2 power-law within 1e-6.
Thermal softening test: at T > Tref (for JC only), yield stress is lower than at T = Tref.
Each test uses the `radial_return` call directly on a single (E, alpha, T) triple — no Newton solve needed.
implementation_steps: Implement each test with clear pass/fail assertions and document the theoretical expectation in the docstring.
Tests are fast (no Taichi, no Newton solve) — no @pytest.mark.slow.
acceptance_criteria: Rate sensitivity monotonic for Perzyna and JC.
Quasi-static limit matches J2 power-law for both models.
risks: `monotonic` is fragile if the curve is flat between two strain rates. Mitigation: use two rates that differ by 3+ orders of magnitude so the signal is unambiguous.

commands.command: uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/ -m 'not slow and not gpu'

completion_notes: Filled all 5 scaffold stubs in test_viscoplastic_acceptance.py with real assertions: Perzyna + JC rate sensitivity, Perzyna + JC quasi-static limits, JC thermal softening.
JC rate sweep uses dt in [1e-3, 1e-7] to keep dl/dt >> eps_dot_0 (otherwise the max(dl/(dt*eps_dot_0), 1) clamp in the flow stress masks rate dependence).
All stress comparisons use deviatoric(stress) before von_mises to isolate the plastic signal from the volumetric elastic component.
Signal floors: >=5% for rate sensitivity (both models), >=10% for thermal softening. Guards against a trivially monotone but essentially flat curve.
Quasi-static limits tested to 1e-6 on both stress and alpha (tighter than the plan's 1e-6 norm).
